description: UniFi Poller - Firewall policy posture for UniFi Network zone-based firewall (Prometheus) plus UniFi firewall blocks and threat detections (Loki). Requires UnPoller v2.37.0+; zone panels require v3.0.0+ and an API key; security events require the Loki output and SAVE_SYSLOG.

panels.description: Total firewall policies defined on the selected site(s), predefined and custom. Source: unpoller_firewall_rules_total.
panels.title: Total rules

targets.expr: sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_total{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})

panels.description: Firewall policies currently enabled. Source: unpoller_firewall_rules_enabled.
panels.title: Enabled

targets.expr: sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_enabled{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})

panels.description: Firewall policies that exist but are switched off. Highlighted when non-zero so forgotten or temporarily disabled rules stand out. Source: unpoller_firewall_rules_disabled.
panels.title: Disabled

targets.expr: sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_disabled{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})

panels.description: Policies whose action is BLOCK or REJECT (enabled or not). Source: unpoller_firewall_rules_by_action.
panels.title: Block / reject rules

targets.expr: sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_by_action{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site",action=~"BLOCK|REJECT"})

panels.description: Policies you created, as opposed to UniFi's predefined zone policies. Source: unpoller_firewall_rules_custom.
panels.title: Custom rules

targets.expr: sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_custom{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})

panels.description: Policies with syslog logging turned on. Source: unpoller_firewall_rules_logging_enabled.
panels.title: Logging enabled

targets.expr: sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_logging_enabled{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})

panels.description: All policies (enabled and disabled) grouped by action. Source: unpoller_firewall_rules_by_action.
panels.title: Rules by action

targets.expr: sum by (action) (unpoller_firewall_rules_by_action{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})

panels.description: UniFi-generated zone policies versus policies you created.
panels.title: Predefined vs custom

targets.expr: sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_predefined{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})
sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_custom{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})

panels.title: Rules enabled
panels.description: Share of policies that are enabled (enabled / total).

targets.expr: 100 * sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_enabled{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"}) / sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_total{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})

panels.title: Rules by protocol
panels.description: Policies grouped by protocol, filtered by the Action and Rule selectors. Counted from per-rule series (unpoller_firewall_rule_enabled); UnPoller merges rules that share an identical name, action, protocol, IP version and zones into one series, so this can be slightly lower than Total Rules.

targets.expr: sort_desc(count by (protocol) (unpoller_firewall_rule_enabled{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site",action=~"$Action",rule_name=~"$Rule"}))

panels.title: Rule inventory over time
panels.description: How the policy set changes over time. Steps in these lines mean someone added, removed, enabled or disabled policies.

targets.expr: sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_total{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})
sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_enabled{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})
sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_disabled{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})
sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_custom{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})
sum(unpoller_firewall_rules_logging_enabled{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"})

panels.title: Changes in selected time range
panels.description: Configuration drift detector for the dashboard's time range. Rule count changes: how often the total number of policies changed. Enable/disable toggles: how often any policy was switched on or off. Priority changes: how often any policy's order changed. Anything above zero that you didn't do yourself deserves a look. Note: adding and removing a policy between two scrapes nets to zero.

targets.expr: sum(changes(unpoller_firewall_rules_total{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"}[$__range]))
sum(changes(unpoller_firewall_rule_enabled{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"}[$__range]))
sum(changes(unpoller_firewall_rule_index{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Firewall policies
panels.description: Every firewall policy, sorted by priority. Use the column filter icons or the Action / Rule selectors at the top. Zones are shown as UniFi zone IDs: UnPoller's policy metrics carry zone IDs, not zone names. Policies that share an identical name, action, protocol, IP version and zones appear as a single row. Zone names come from a fixed ID-to-name map for this controller; a zone created later shows as its ID until it is added to the map.

targets.expr: max by (rule_name, action, protocol, ip_version, source_zone, dest_zone, site_name, source) (unpoller_firewall_rule_enabled{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site",action=~"$Action",rule_name=~"$Rule"})

max by (rule_name, action, protocol, ip_version, source_zone, dest_zone, site_name, source) (unpoller_firewall_rule_index{source=~"$Controller",site_name=~"$Site",action=~"$Action",rule_name=~"$Rule"})

panels.title: Blocked connections
panels.description: Connections blocked by a firewall policy in the selected time range. Source: UniFi System Log 'Blocked by Firewall' entries, pushed to Loki by UnPoller. UniFi does not include ports or protocol in these entries.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({application="unifi_system_log", category="SECURITY", source=~"$Controller", site_name=~"$Site"} |= `"subcategory":"SECURITY_FIREWALL"` | json sub="subcategory", policy="parameters.TRIGGER.name", sip="parameters.SRC_IP.name", scl="parameters.SRC_CLIENT.name", sclip="parameters.SRC_CLIENT.ip", dip="parameters.DST_IP.name", ddev="parameters.DST_DEVICE.name" | sub="SECURITY_FIREWALL" | label_format src=`{{ or .scl .sip }}`, srcaddr=`{{ or .sclip .sip }}`, dst=`{{ or .ddev .dip }}` [$__range]))

panels.title: From the internet
panels.description: Blocks whose source is a public address, typically scanners and bots probing your public IPs. Source: UniFi System Log 'Blocked by Firewall' entries, pushed to Loki by UnPoller. UniFi does not include ports or protocol in these entries.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({application="unifi_system_log", category="SECURITY", source=~"$Controller", site_name=~"$Site"} |= `"subcategory":"SECURITY_FIREWALL"` | json sub="subcategory", policy="parameters.TRIGGER.name", sip="parameters.SRC_IP.name", scl="parameters.SRC_CLIENT.name", sclip="parameters.SRC_CLIENT.ip", dip="parameters.DST_IP.name", ddev="parameters.DST_DEVICE.name" | sub="SECURITY_FIREWALL" | label_format src=`{{ or .scl .sip }}`, srcaddr=`{{ or .sclip .sip }}`, dst=`{{ or .ddev .dip }}` | srcaddr !~ `(10|127)\..*|192\.168\..*|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\..*|f[cd][0-9a-f]{2}:.*|fe80:.*` [$__range]))

panels.title: From your network
panels.description: Blocks whose source is a private address inside your network (a device or VLAN hitting a block policy). Worth a look: often a misconfigured device, sometimes a policy that is too strict. Source: UniFi System Log 'Blocked by Firewall' entries, pushed to Loki by UnPoller. UniFi does not include ports or protocol in these entries.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({application="unifi_system_log", category="SECURITY", source=~"$Controller", site_name=~"$Site"} |= `"subcategory":"SECURITY_FIREWALL"` | json sub="subcategory", policy="parameters.TRIGGER.name", sip="parameters.SRC_IP.name", scl="parameters.SRC_CLIENT.name", sclip="parameters.SRC_CLIENT.ip", dip="parameters.DST_IP.name", ddev="parameters.DST_DEVICE.name" | sub="SECURITY_FIREWALL" | label_format src=`{{ or .scl .sip }}`, srcaddr=`{{ or .sclip .sip }}`, dst=`{{ or .ddev .dip }}` | srcaddr =~ `(10|127)\..*|192\.168\..*|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\..*|f[cd][0-9a-f]{2}:.*|fe80:.*` [$__range]))

panels.title: Unique blocked sources
panels.description: Number of different sources (IPs or devices) that were blocked in the selected time range. Source: UniFi System Log 'Blocked by Firewall' entries, pushed to Loki by UnPoller. UniFi does not include ports or protocol in these entries.

targets.expr: count(sum by (src) (count_over_time({application="unifi_system_log", category="SECURITY", source=~"$Controller", site_name=~"$Site"} |= `"subcategory":"SECURITY_FIREWALL"` | json sub="subcategory", policy="parameters.TRIGGER.name", sip="parameters.SRC_IP.name", scl="parameters.SRC_CLIENT.name", sclip="parameters.SRC_CLIENT.ip", dip="parameters.DST_IP.name", ddev="parameters.DST_DEVICE.name" | sub="SECURITY_FIREWALL" | label_format src=`{{ or .scl .sip }}`, srcaddr=`{{ or .sclip .sip }}`, dst=`{{ or .ddev .dip }}` [$__range])))

sum(count_over_time({application="unifi_system_log", category="SECURITY", source=~"$Controller", site_name=~"$Site"} |= `"subcategory":"SECURITY_FIREWALL"` | json sub="subcategory", policy="parameters.TRIGGER.name", sip="parameters.SRC_IP.name", scl="parameters.SRC_CLIENT.name", sclip="parameters.SRC_CLIENT.ip", dip="parameters.DST_IP.name", ddev="parameters.DST_DEVICE.name" | sub="SECURITY_FIREWALL" | label_format src=`{{ or .scl .sip }}`, srcaddr=`{{ or .sclip .sip }}`, dst=`{{ or .ddev .dip }}` | srcaddr =~ `(10|127)\..*|192\.168\..*|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\..*|f[cd][0-9a-f]{2}:.*|fe80:.*` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Threats detected
panels.description: All threat detections in the selected time range. Source: UniFi System Log Security entries other than firewall blocks (intrusion prevention/detection, honeypot), pushed to Loki by UnPoller. These entries name the clients involved (or their MAC address when UniFi has no name for them) but carry no IP addresses, signature or threat category; see Insights > Inspection in UniFi for those details.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({application="unifi_system_log", category="SECURITY", source=~"$Controller", site_name=~"$Site"} != `"subcategory":"SECURITY_FIREWALL"` | json sub="subcategory", evt="event", scl="parameters.SRC_CLIENT.name", sip="parameters.SRC_IP.name", dcl="parameters.DST_CLIENT.name", dip="parameters.DST_IP.name", ddev="parameters.DST_DEVICE.name" | sub!="SECURITY_FIREWALL" | label_format src=`{{ or .scl .sip }}`, dst=`{{ or .dcl .dip .ddev }}`, type=`{{ regexReplaceAll "_" (regexReplaceAll "^SECURITY_" .sub "") " " }}` [$__range]))

panels.title: Threat clients: MAC to IP lookup
panels.description: Every client MAC involved in a threat, matched to the IP, name and network UniFi reported for that MAC during the selected time range (from UnPoller's client metrics). Several rows for one MAC mean its IP changed during the range. 'not found' means UniFi never listed that MAC as a client in this range: UniFi devices (gateway, switches, APs), very short connections, a private/randomized MAC that has since changed, or data older than Prometheus keeps (15 days by default). Treat the match as a strong clue, not proof. Source: UniFi System Log Security entries other than firewall blocks (intrusion prevention/detection, honeypot), pushed to Loki by UnPoller. These entries name the clients involved (or their MAC address when UniFi has no name for them) but carry no IP addresses, signature or threat category; see Insights > Inspection in UniFi for those details.

options.content:
### What the numbers mean

Each bar is a firewall zone. The number is **how many networks (VLANs / subnets) are assigned to it**.

- **Internal, Guest-Zone, DNS, Blackhole, untrust**: your LAN networks, grouped by the zone you put them in
- **External**: your WAN connections, one per internet uplink or WAN-side network
- **Vpn**: VPN server networks
- **Gateway**: the UDM itself, always 0 because no network belongs to it
- **Hotspot, Dmz**: built-in zones you are not using yet

Zones you created yourself are *user defined*, the rest come with UniFi. Firewall policies are written between zones, so the *Source zone* and *Destination zone* columns in the Firewall policies table refer to these same zones.

A count that changes means a network was moved between zones. A zone at 0 has no networks, so its policies match nothing.

<small>Source: UniFi Integration API through UnPoller (needs `UP_UNIFI_CONTROLLER_0_API_KEY`).</small>
